These assertions encode the old device's own rule that the pixel-mode select, not the copy's base words, decides whether a copy touches the id plane or the colour buffer. Base words are board addresses: OpenBSD sends 0x2000, the screen base, and the recorded signed-texture upload copies from a scratch address that is not the selected base (odsy devices/buzz/measured.md section 10, software expectation). No source supports the old rule; what the board does for a base that disagrees with the select is unknown.

The old device took the id plane to be wherever the last select named. The id plane is the memory the display's overlay base register points at (0x142000 here, odsy devices/buzz/measured.md section 3); a select or copy base elsewhere names other memory. The old test source calls the rule model policy and unknown. No value is asserted for a relocated select.

Run 5 sets header word 7 bit 10, the unpack byte-swap flag (odsy devices/buzz/pixel-paths.md header table, inferred from the library). GL's byte swap reverses multi-byte elements, and this header's type is bytes, so the draw proceeds and the pixel is written; the old device refused every swap draw because its effect was unknown. Later runs (size field 3, size-code mismatch) cannot be judged after the pixel is written, so no value is asserted between them.
